581: B is correct because setting the Auto Scaling group minimum capacity to four, with two On-Demand Instances in each of two Availability Zones, guarantees that at least two instances remain running even if an entire Availability Zone fails. This design provides high availability and fault tolerance at the Availability Zone level, and On-Demand Instances run without the interruption risk of Spot Instances. A minimum capacity of only two would leave a single healthy instance during an AZ outage until replacements launch.
582: A is correct because a Route 53 geolocation routing policy routes DNS traffic based on the geographic location of the users, sending traffic near the on-premises data center in us-west-1 to the on-premises site and traffic near eu-central-1 to the AWS Region. Serving each user group from its closest endpoint minimizes website load time. Simple and weighted routing policies cannot make location-based routing decisions.
583: C is correct because shipping Snowball devices avoids transferring 5 PB of tape data over the 1 Gbps uplink, which would take far longer than the six-month migration window. Tape Gateway on Snowball lets the company copy its physical tapes to virtual tapes on the device without building extra staging infrastructure. A lifecycle policy then moves the archived tapes to S3 Glacier Deep Archive, the lowest-cost storage class, which is ideal for compliance data retained for 10 years.
584: A is correct because a spread placement group places each EC2 instance on a distinct underlying rack with its own power and network, ensuring that no group of nodes shares the same physical hardware. This isolates the parallel data-processing nodes so a single hardware failure cannot affect them all. Dedicated tenancy still allows instances from the same account to share a dedicated host, and separate accounts do not control host placement.
585: D is correct because an EC2 Capacity Reservation reserves compute capacity in a specific Availability Zone of the failover Region for as long as needed, guaranteeing that capacity is actually available when a disaster recovery failover occurs. On-Demand Instances, Savings Plans, and Reserved Instances provide pricing or billing benefits but do not guarantee capacity will be available on demand in the failover Region. Only a Capacity Reservation directly satisfies the requirement to meet capacity in the failover Region.
586: B is correct because an AWS account can belong to only one organization at a time, so the R&D account must first leave the prior organization and can then be invited into the new organization from the new management account. Inviting the existing account preserves its resources, configurations, and account identity during the separation. Keeping the account in both organizations simultaneously is not possible, and creating a new account would force a costly resource migration.
587: C is correct because an Amazon API Gateway endpoint integrates easily with other web applications and automatically scales to absorb sudden, unpredictable bursts of customer activity. Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose reliably buffers and delivers the captured events into an Amazon S3 bucket for analytics and downstream predictions. An API Gateway Lambda authorizer supplies the required authorization step before requests reach the backend, whereas a Gateway Load Balancer is designed for inline security appliances rather than API authorization.
588: D is correct because a 24-hour RPO and RTO can be met by copying the existing automatic RDS snapshots to another Region once per day, which provides a restorable point-in-time copy in a disaster. This is the most cost-effective approach because it reuses the automated backups and incurs only snapshot storage and cross-Region transfer costs. A cross-Region read replica or DMS replication provides far tighter RPO than required and adds continuous replication costs.
589: B is correct because ElastiCache for Redis supports Multi-AZ deployment with automatic failover and replication, so session state stored in Redis survives the loss of any web server. Moving the session state out of the web servers removes the dependency on sticky sessions and on the health of a single instance, delivering the required high availability. Memcached does not offer automatic failover or persistence, and Storage Gateway or RDS introduce higher latency and cost for session data.
590: A is correct because an RDS for MySQL read replica offloads the once-a-month report queries to a separate instance, keeping the primary DB instance, which is sized for the average daily workload, free from contention. The read replica can be created and deleted around the reporting window, so the company pays for the extra capacity only when needed. Resizing would permanently pay for peak capacity, and restoring backups or exporting to S3 adds manual effort and stale data.
591: B is correct because the AWS Load Balancer Controller provisions an Application Load Balancer that integrates with Kubernetes Ingress resources to perform layer-7 path-based routing, directing each request to the correct microservice such as customers or orders. The ALB is a fully managed service that scales automatically without extra compute for the routing tier. A Network Load Balancer works at layer 4 and cannot route by URL path, and API Gateway or Lambda in front of EKS adds cost and complexity.
592: D is correct because Amazon S3 provides durable, low-cost object storage for the images, while Amazon CloudFront caches them at edge locations worldwide so the global customer base gets fast access. CloudFront geographic restrictions deny requests that originate from the specified countries, meeting the blocking requirement. Signed URLs give each customer controlled, time-limited access to the copyrighted content, whereas public buckets, per-customer IAM users, and per-country EC2 fleets either fail the restrictions or cost far more.
593: A is correct because a Multi-AZ ElastiCache for Redis replication group provides automatic failover from a primary to a replica in a different Availability Zone, protecting against node-level and AZ-level failures within the Region. Shards that contain multiple nodes add replication so the loss of a single node does not cause performance degradation or data loss. AOF persistence, additional read replicas, and Auto Scaling do not by themselves deliver cross-AZ automatic failover.
594: C is correct because EC2 hibernation saves the contents of instance memory to the EBS root volume when the instance is stopped, so on relaunch the application resumes from its preloaded state instead of repeating the long startup and memory-loading process. Auto Scaling warm pools keep these paused, pre-initialized instances ready to enter service almost immediately during the next testing phase. The other options address capacity availability but do not reduce the long launch and memory initialization time.
595: C is correct because dynamic scaling automatically adjusts the size of the Auto Scaling group in response to real-time metrics such as CPU utilization or request count, so capacity grows whenever a sudden traffic increase occurs on any random day. This maintains application performance during unpredictable spikes without paying for idle capacity the rest of the time. Predictive and scheduled scaling rely on recurring patterns, and manual scaling cannot respond quickly enough to unexpected surges.
596: A is correct because Aurora Serverless v2 automatically and continuously scales database capacity in fine-grained increments, instantly handling the unpredictable connection and load spikes during the monthly sales events. Because the company pays only for the capacity actually used, the database scales down between events, making it the most cost-effective option. A larger EC2 or RDS instance is paid for around the clock, and Redshift is an analytics warehouse rather than an OLTP engine for an ecommerce application.
597: B is correct because scheduled scaling of Lambda provisioned concurrency pre-initializes the required execution environments before employees begin using the application each day, eliminating the cold-start latency they currently experience. Provisioned concurrency keeps functions warm and ready to respond immediately, and scheduling it to the daily usage pattern avoids paying for it around the clock. Raising the throttling limit or function memory does not prevent cold starts, and a CloudWatch alarm adds operational overhead without pre-warming the functions.
598: A is correct because deploying AWS Storage Gateway in Amazon S3 File Gateway mode provides an on-premises SMB file share that transparently writes the .csv files from the devices into Amazon S3, matching the devices' SMB capability without custom code. C is correct because an AWS Glue crawler scans the data in S3 and creates the table definition in the AWS Glue Data Catalog so the files can be queried with SQL. F is correct because Amazon Athena is a serverless service that runs standard SQL directly against the S3 data, and its pay-per-query pricing is the most cost-effective option for periodic queries throughout the day.
599: A is correct because with AWS Outposts the customer must provide resilient power and network connectivity to the Outposts racks, since the infrastructure runs in the customer's own facility. C is correct because the customer remains responsible for the physical security and access controls of the data center environment that hosts the racks. F is correct because the customer is responsible for capacity planning, including providing extra Amazon ECS cluster capacity to absorb server failures and maintenance events. AWS manages the Outposts infrastructure itself, including the hypervisor, storage systems, power supplies, servers, networking equipment, and physical maintenance of rack components.
600: A is correct because a Network Load Balancer operates at layer 4, is designed to handle millions of requests per second, and maintains ultra-low latency, matching the 3 million requests per second requirement on the nonstandard TCP port. The NLB exposes a public listener on the required TCP port and forwards traffic to the TCP application inside the VPC. An ALB is optimized for layer 7 HTTP traffic, and CloudFront and API Gateway do not support listeners on arbitrary TCP ports.
